STEM.value: You grow toward the light you believe in — even where nothing shelters you.
You bend where others break — and call it nothing, though it is everything.
You warm every room you enter — and rarely ask who warms you.
You keep a small fire no storm has found — others read by its light.
You hold what others set down — so long, they forget the weight was theirs.
Everything you tend grows — you are the last to call it your harvest.
You say what others soften — and pay, quietly, for being the one who did.
You were polished by what pressed you — brilliance is the part that survived.
You hold more than anyone thinks to ask about — depth was never meant to be seen.
You change things slowly, softly, completely — and let the credit fall elsewhere.
